description: The sandbox tree's pods explode with a gunshot crack, launching seeds at about 70 metres per second. #shorts #nature #facts #didyouknow

title: The garden flower that poisons through your skin #shorts
description: Aconite, or wolfsbane, contains aconitine, a toxin that can be absorbed through the skin and stop the heart. #shorts #nature #facts #didyouknow
script: One of the deadliest plants in Europe grows in ordinary gardens. Aconite, also called monkshood or wolfsbane, has pretty purple flowers. Every part contains aconitine. It jams the body's nerve and heart cells in the on position. First your mouth and skin tingle and go numb. Then come vomiting and a racing, chaotic heartbeat. The toxin can even absorb through the skin, which is why gardeners are told to wear gloves.

title: A fungus killed 25 million trees in one country #shorts
description: Dutch elm disease, carried by bark beetles, killed around 25 million of Britain's elms after the late 1960s. #shorts #nature #facts #didyouknow
script: A fungus killed about twenty-five million trees in Britain alone. Dutch elm disease is carried by bark beetles that tunnel under elm bark. The fungus spreads into the tree's water pipes. title: The mould that caused a famine #shorts
description: Phytophthora infestans rotted Ireland's potatoes from 1845, leading to the Great Famine in which about a million people died. #shorts #nature #facts #didyouknow
script: A microscopic water mould killed about a million people. In 1845, Phytophthora infestans reached Ireland. It spread through potato fields on wet wind. Healthy green plants turned black within days, and the potatoes rotted into stinking mush in the ground. Millions of people depended on potatoes almost entirely. The blight returned year after year. Around a million died of hunger and disease, and another million left the country.

title: The parasite that gives frogs extra legs #shorts

script: A parasite gives frogs extra legs so birds can eat them. Ribeiroia is a flatworm. Its larvae burrow into tadpoles right where the back legs are growing. The cysts scramble the limb buds. title: The parasite that makes trout chase their tails #shorts
description: Whirling disease damages young trout skeletons so they swim in circles; it wiped out about 90 percent of rainbow trout in parts of Montana. #shorts #nature #facts #didyouknow
script: A parasite makes young trout chase their own tails until they die. Whirling disease eats the soft cartilage of baby fish while their skeletons are still forming. Nerves get pinched, and the fish swim in frantic circles. Their tails turn black and their skulls grow twisted. They can't feed or escape. In the 1990s, it wiped out about ninety percent of the rainbow trout in parts of Montana's Madison River.

title: Some adult mayflies live less than five minutes #shorts
description: Adult mayflies have no working mouth, and females of one American species live less than five minutes after emerging. #shorts #nature #facts #didyouknow
script: Some adult mayflies live less than five minutes. Mayflies spend up to two years underwater as nymphs. Then they emerge as adults with no working mouth and a gut full of air. They can't eat. Their only job is to mate. Females of one American species, Dolania americana, emerge before dawn, mate, drop their eggs into the river, and die in under five minutes. Fish below are waiting for them.
